personal.name: Chandra Sreeja
personal.title: Master's in Computer Science @ UIUC
bio: I'm a Data Engineer and Master's Student at UIUC. I enjoy turning messy data into meaningful insights, automating workflows, and solving real-world problems.
Currently a Data Engineering Intern at ADM and Master's student at UIUC with past experience at Barclays developing ETL pipelines, data models, and credit risk analytics.
Beyond work, I've conducted research with Dr. Naiman Khan at UIUC on large-scale public health and nutrition datasets.

research.title: Graduate Researcher — SMARTHUB
points: Worked with large USDA food and nutrient datasets alongside Illinois school-level meal-plan data to support research on the nutritional value of foods provided through school meal programs.
Cleaned, transformed, and structured heterogeneous datasets from multiple sources to make them suitable for integrated, downstream statistical analysis.
Examined dataset schemas, variables, and cross-source relationships across food, nutrient, meal, and school-level information.
Applied Python, Pandas, NumPy, and SQL-based data processing techniques to organize, sanitize, and query large datasets.
Developed solutions for integrating public datasets with varying schemas, structures, and levels of granularity.

featuredProjects.title: PACT: Pruned Agent Call Throughput
featuredProjects.subtitle: Predicting Early Exit Points in Autonomous Agent Reasoning Chains
featuredProjects.description: Designed and engineered an LLM-based system to significantly reduce latency in autonomous agents by predicting early exit points in reasoning chains. Implemented and fine-tuned a Phi-3-mini-based classifier to predict task readiness and dynamically prune unnecessary intermediate reasoning steps, achieving 71% readiness prediction accuracy.

featuredProjects.title: Wildfire Image Classification System
featuredProjects.subtitle: Deep Learning & Transfer Learning for Image Classification
featuredProjects.description: Developed a deep learning image classification system to distinguish wildfire images from fall foliage using pretrained ResNet-18 and ResNet-101 architectures. Performed transfer learning and fine-tuning to adapt the models to the target dataset, with image preprocessing, model training, and performance evaluation.
